sources.entry: Convoker - Type an app name, press Enter, all its windows come to you. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/varie-ai/convoker) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: Convoker is a macOS menu bar app that gathers all windows of a chosen app onto your current screen via a fuzzy-search command palette.
summary.what_it_does: Convoker runs in the macOS menu bar and opens a floating command palette (opened with Cmd+Shift+X) where you type an app name. Enter gathers all of that app's windows to the current screen in a grid, and Shift+Enter gathers and maximizes them. Cmd+Enter activates an app and hides the others, and Tab pins up to four apps for side-by-side split layouts. Workspaces save an app arrangement under a name so that typing the name launches apps, arranges windows, and hides distractions, including across multiple monitors. Layout options include grid, cascade, side-by-side, and columns. It uses the macOS Accessibility API to enumerate and reposition windows.
use_cases: Bring scattered windows of one app to the current screen
Focus on one app and hide everything else
Split two or more apps side-by-side
Save and restore a named app arrangement workspace
Launch an app and auto-arrange its windows
Quick app switching from a keyboard palette
how_to_run: git clone <repository URL from README; left blank in the README>
Alternatively, download the latest .dmg from Releases and drag Convoker.app to /Applications
Launch Convoker and grant Accessibility permission when prompted
Press Cmd+Shift+X to open the palette
notable: Operates on all windows of an app at once, rather than snapping individual windows
On-demand: no background daemons, no config files, never rearranges windows automatically
Named workspaces that launch apps, arrange windows, and hide others across monitors
Configurable global hotkey via tray Settings
Universal binary for Apple Silicon and Intel
caveats: Needs Accessibility permission to discover and move windows
Works best with Stage Manager disabled
